'''Melody S. Goodman''' is an American biostatistician and higher education executive whose work focuses on [[social determinants of health]], [[health literacy]], and [[stakeholder engagement]] in health research.{{r|nyu}}<ref>{{Cite web |date=2021-09-24 |title=Melody Goodman, PhD, MS {{!}} PCORI |url=https://www.pcori.org/people/melody-goodman-phd-ms |access-date=2024-08-31 |website=www.pcori.org |language=en}}</ref><ref name=":0">{{Cite web |last=Varker |first=Abby |date=2024-03-25 |title=Alumna Melody S. Goodman interviewd in Boston University's Public Health Post |url=https://www.hsph.harvard.edu/biostatistics/2024/03/alumna-melody-s-goodman-interviewd-in-boston-universitys-public-health-post/ |access-date=2024-08-31 |website=Harvard University Department of Biostatistics |language=en-us}}</ref> Goodman has spoken publicly about racial disparities in access to healthcare,{{r|usnews|cbs}} and is an advocate for public outreach and engagement on health issues.{{r|priority|newsday}} She is a professor of biostatistics and Dean of the [https://publichealth.nyu.edu/ New York University School of Global Public Health] as of 2025.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Melody Goodman {{!}} NYU School of Global Public Health |url=https://publichealth.nyu.edu/faculty/melody-goodman |access-date=2024-04-03 |website=publichealth.nyu.edu |language=en}}</ref> 

==Education and career==
Goodman majored in economics and applied mathematics & statistics as an undergraduate at [[Stony Brook University]],{{r|nyu}} graduating in 1999.{{r|sbcv}} She went to [[Harvard University]] for graduate study in [[biostatistics]],{{r|nyu}} earning a master's degree in 2003 and completing her Ph.D. in 2006.{{r|sbcv}} Her dissertation, ''Statistical Methods for Community-Based Cancer Interventions and Health Disparities Research'', was supervised by Yi Li.{{r|mg}} She is [[African-American]], but had no African-American professors throughout her education, and her later publications have included work on the diversity of students and faculty in public health.{{r|diverse}}

Goodman taught biostatistics at Stony Brook University,{{r|bookbio}} where she was an assistant professor of preventive medicine,{{r|sbcv}}  [[Washington University School of Medicine]],{{r|bookbio}} where she was an assistant professor in the Division of Public Health Sciences, and [[New York University]].{{r|wustl}} Goodman has been a member of the NYU Global Public Health faculty since 2017.<ref name=":1" /><ref name=":0" /> 

On March 29, 2024, Goodman was named Interim Dean of the NYU School of Global Public Health after [[Debra Furr-Holden]] stepped down from the deanship.<ref name=":1">{{Cite web |last=Communications |first=NYU Web |title=Debra Furr-Holden Stepping Down, and the Appointment of Melody Goodman as Interim Dean |url=http://www.nyu.edu/content/nyu/en/about/leadership-university-administration/office-of-the-president/comms/debra-furr-holden-stepping-down-appointment-melody-goodman-as-interim-dean |access-date=2024-04-01 |website=www.nyu.edu |language=en}}</ref> 

==Books==
Goodman is the author of the book ''Biostatistics for Clinical and Public Health Research'' (Routledge, 2018).{{r|mahmood}} With Vetta Sanders Thompson, she is co-editor of ''Public Health Research Methods for Partnerships and Practice'' (Routledge, 2018).

==Recognition==
Goodman was named a [[Fellow of the American Statistical Association]] in 2021.{{r|fasa}}
